defs.def: to point away from the centre 向外；朝外
to be discovered to be; to prove to be 原来是；证明是；结果是

ex.s: General knowledge can at times turn out to be true.
ex.t: 常识有时可能被证明是正确的。

ex.s: They turned out largely ineffective.
ex.t: 它们最终在很大程度上是无效的。

ex.s: A bright spot for me turned out to be reading.
ex.t: 对我来说，一个亮点原来是阅读。

ex.s: So that’s what I did, and it turned out Dad was right.
ex.t: 于是我就这么做了，结果证明爸爸是对的。

ex.s: It turns out that pet transporting pays quite well at about $30, 000 per year before tax.
ex.t: 事实证明宠物运输报酬相当可观，税前每年约30,000美元。

ex.s: The games my parents taught me where I was a child turned out to be very useful later in my life.
ex.t: 我小时候父母教我的游戏，后来在我生活中证明非常有用。

ex.s: As it turns out, however, this same concept-one that most consumers make many times each day with reflecting on it-is the basis of the more formal budget line concept in economics , which is explained below.
ex.t: 然而，事实证明，同一个概念——大多数消费者每天都会做出许多次、却不去反思的概念——是经济学中更正式的预算线概念的基础，下文将作解释。

defs.def: to switch a light or a source of heat off 关掉（灯或热源）；熄灭

ex.s: Thankfully, Jeff stayed calm and turned off the gas quickly.
ex.t: 庆幸的是，杰夫保持冷静，迅速关掉了燉气。

ex.s: Thankfully, Jeff stayed calm and turned off the gas quickly.
ex.t: 庆幸的是，杰夫保持冷静，迅速关掉了燉气。

ex.s: Next, Jeff turned on the second stove burner to heat up the frying pan.
ex.t: 接下来，杰夫打开第二个炉灶燃烧器，加热煎锅。

ex.s: Next, Jeff turned on the second stove burner to heat up the frying pan.
ex.t: 接下来，杰夫打开第二个炉灶燃烧器，加热煎锅。

defs.def: to clean sth thoroughly by removing the contents and organizing them again 腾空；彻底清理
to empty sth, especially your pockets 弄空，掏净（尤指口袋）
to make sth point away from the centre 使向外；使朝外
to change position so that the other side is facing towards the outside or the top 翻身；翻转
to start or to continue to run 发动机

ex.s: I realized that years of living as a late-night person had turned my heart into an overworked engine.
ex.t: 我意识到，多年熬夜的生活已经把我的心变成了一台过度运转的发动机。

defs.def: to change to another channel when you are watching television 变换（电视频道）

ex.s: Before turning to the economics definition of budget line, consider another concept: the line-item budget.
ex.t: 这种用法没有什么复杂的地方，预算线就是预算中的一行，上面注明了要购买的服务或商品及其成本，

defs.def: to make sth change position so that the other side is facing towards the outside or the top 使翻个儿；使翻转
to think about sth carefully 认真思考；深思熟虑
to sell goods and replace them 商店
to steal from a place 从 … 偷窃

ex.s: Turner wisely said that “doing well” psychologically is being able to roll with the flow of emotions, manage them, communicate clearly and well with others, and master various skills.
ex.t: 特纳明智地说，“从心理上讲”“做得好”是能够顺应情绪的流动，管理情绪，与他人清晰良好地沟通，并掌握各种技能。“

ex.s: Without the education I was throwing away, I’d turn to theft and go to prison.
ex.t: 没有我正在抛弃的教育，我会走上偷窃的道路，然后进监狱。

defs.def: to make an engine start running 发动（引擎）

ex.s: I tried to turn on my brain but the engine just wouldn't start.” I should say my name, of course.
ex.t: “我试图启动我的大脑，可引擎就是打不着火。”当然，我应该说我的名字。

defs.def: to be found, especially by chance, after being lost （尤指失去后偶然）被发现，被找到

ex.s: But recently it has discovered that data can be turned into new services: translation and visual recognition, to be sold to other companies.
ex.t: 但最近它发现数据可以被转化为新服务：翻译和视觉识别，然后出售给其他公司。

defs.def: to arrive 人

ex.s: By the time 250,000 were on the bridge, engineers noticed something terrible：the roadway was flattening under what turned out to be the heaviest load it had ever been asked to carry.
ex.t: 等到25万人在桥上时，工程师们注意到一件可怕的事情：桥面在它迄今承载的最重负荷下变平了。

ex.s: Some will turn out to their parents or teachers for help.
ex.t: 他们的回答也表明他们不喜欢和别人交谈。

ex.s: With any luck, he’ll turn a few more heads in the process.
ex.t: 运气好的话，他在此过程中还会吸引更多人的目光。

ex.s: When we turn on a light or switch on a TV or a computer we use energy and we need water to produce this energy.
ex.t: 事实是我们很幸运无论何时想要都有干净的水，但这对于世界上许多人来说并非如此。

defs.def: to happen, especially by chance 机会
to increase the sound, heat, etc. of a piece of equipment 开大，调高（音量、热量等）

ex.s: The piece of bread in the pan had turned black as well.
ex.t: 锅里的那片面包也变黑了。

ex.s: The piece of bread in the pan had turned black as well.
ex.t: 锅里的那片面包也变黑了。

defs.def: to make a piece of clothing shorter by folding and sewing it up at the bottom 将（衣服的底边）折起缝好；改短

ex.s: The yellow and orange stone fruits such as peaches are high in the carotenoids we turn into vitamin A and which are antioxidants.
ex.t: 桃子等黄色和橙色核果富含类胡萝卜素，我们将其转化为维生素A，且它们是抗氧化剂。

ex.s: It will be turned into a museum.
ex.t: 它将被改造成一座博物馆。

ex.s: When I was 17， I read a magazine article about a museum called the McNay， once the home of a watercolorist named Marian McNay． She had requested the community to turn it into a museum upon her death． On a sunny Saturday， Sally and I drove over to the museum． She asked， "Do you have the address？ ""No， but I'll recognize it， there was a picture in the magazine．
ex.t: 我17岁时，读到一篇杂志文章，介绍一家叫麦克奈的博物馆，它曾是水彩画家玛丽安·麦克奈的故居。她曾要求社区在她去世后将其改为博物馆。一个阳光明媚的周六，萨莉和我开车去了博物馆。她问："你有地址吗？""没有，但我会认出来的，杂志上有照片。"

ex.s: Curtin is CEO of DC Central Kitchen in Washington, D.C., which recovers food and turns it into healthy meals.
ex.t: Curtin是华盛顿特区DC Central Kitchen的首席执行官，该公司回收食物并将其转化为健康餐食。

defs.def: to find sth 找到；发现

ex.s: Yet, when something new turns up, more often than not, we do not even know its name.
ex.t: 然而，当新事物出现时，我们往往甚至不知道它的名字。

ex.s: It turns out that baby red-backed fairy wrens also emerge chirping like their moms.
ex.t: 结果发现，红背细尾鹩莺幼鸟孵化出来时也会像妈妈一样啁啾。

ex.s: We'd come down in the morning to find they'd turned the room upside down, and left it looking like a zoo.
ex.t: 我们早上下楼时发现他们把房间弄得乱七八糟，让它看起来像个大动物园。

defs.def: an act of turning sb/sth around 转动；旋动

ex.s: It’s turning to a bunch of high school kids.
ex.t: 它正求助于一群高中生。

defs.def: a change in direction in a vehicle （车辆的）转弯，转向

ex.s: She turned from person to person until she came to me.
ex.t: 她从一个人转向另一个人，直到来到我面前。

ex.s: They turned to overseas markets.
ex.t: 它们转向了海外市场。

ex.s: I am, in part, an ant biologist, so my thoughts turned to what we know about insect life and I knew that much in the world of insects remains unknown.
ex.t: 我在某种程度上是个蚂蚁生物学家，所以我的思绪转向我们对昆虫生命的认知，而我知道昆虫世界中仍有许多未知。

ex.s: Turn to his English teacher.
ex.t: 求助他的英语老师。

ex.s: The boy’s mother turned to the dog, “Okay, Poppy, time to go back home.”
ex.t: 男孩的母亲转向狗说：“好了，Poppy，该回家了。”

defs.def: a place where a road leads away from the one you are travelling on 岔路口；拐弯处；转弯处
a bend or corner in a road （道路的）弯道，转弯处

ex.s: Pahlsson and her husband  62   (search) the kitchen, checking every corner, but turned up nothing.
ex.t: 帕尔松和丈夫   62   （搜索）了厨房，检查每个角落，却一无所获。

defs.def: the time when sb in a group of people should or is allowed to do sth （依次轮到的）机会

ex.s: For Canaan Elementary’s second grade in Patchogue, N.Y.，today is speech day ,and right now it’s Chris Palaez’s turn.
ex.t: 对于纽约州帕乔格市卡南小学二年级来说，今天是演讲日，现在轮到克里斯·帕拉兹了。

defs.def: an unusual or unexpected change in what is happening （异乎寻常或意外的）变化，转变

ex.s: But in some waters，such as those of the Arctic，a warming will make conditions riper for phytoplankton，and these areas will turn greener.
ex.t: 但在某些水域，如北极海域，变暖将使浮游植物的生长条件更加成熟，这些区域将变得更绿。

defs.def: a short performance or piece of entertainment such as a song, etc. 短小节目
a short walk 散步；转一圈
a feeling of illness （疾病的）一阵发作；不适感
one after the other in a particular order 依次；轮流；逐个
as a result of sth in a series of events 相应地；转而
